claims.text: The identity of X in CrFeCoNiX controls protective-scale formation by changing elemental segregation and oxide-metal interface structure.
In CrFeCoNiAl, Al segregates to the oxide-metal interface and promotes a thin, continuous, low-stress alumina-rich or Al-Cr mixed oxide.
In CrFeCoNiSi, Si segregates to the oxide-metal interface and promotes a thin, continuous, low-stress silica-rich or Si-Cr mixed oxide.
A dense external oxide layer can produce protective behavior and slower, parabolic oxidation kinetics.
Alumina- or silica-rich scales repair minor damage during exposure.
Mn is preferentially oxidized in CrMnFeCoNi and its oxidation depletes Mn from the bulk alloy.
Oxidation of CrMnFeCoNi produces non-protective Mn-containing oxides.
Mn-containing CrFeCoNiX tends to form spinel-type oxide under atmospheric oxidation.
The Mn-containing scale grows rapidly and becomes thicker than the Al- or Si-containing scales.
Preferential Mn oxidation and Mn depletion cause poor scale adhesion, cracking, and spallation.
Scale integrity is governed by adhesion, density, defect density, X segregation, and formation of a stable bonding network with Cr.
Alpha-alumina and silica-rich compounds formed in these alloys have a small lattice mismatch with the substrate.
Compressive stress in the Al- or Si-derived oxide heals minor defects and sustains a protective barrier.
Above 900 °C, CrFeCoNi alloys containing Al or Si will retain thin, adherent, slow-growing scales without spallation for prolonged exposure.
Above 900 °C, the Mn-containing alloy will exhibit a thicker, less coherent scale with cracking or spallation.
A CrFeCoNi baseline without X will form a less stable oxide scale than the Al- or Si-containing alloys.
The proposed behavior applies over hundreds of hours above 900 °C in oxidative or corrosive service atmospheres.
Multiphase microstructures may alter oxidation through their effects on diffusion paths and stress distribution.
Compositionally matched alloys with similar microstructural states and identical exposures provide the controlled comparison for isolating the effect of X.
Failure of the Al- or Si-containing alloys to outperform both Mn-containing and baseline alloys in scale coherence, adhesion, and growth kinetics would falsify the hypothesis.
